newsitem.title: CYPRUS: East Mediterranean rocked by earthquake.
newsitem.headline: East Mediterranean rocked by earthquake.

text.p: Drivers abandoned cars and residents ran into the streets screaming on Wednesday when a powerful tremor rocked the east Mediterranean shaking tall buildings.
The British Geological Survey said the tremor registered 6.5 on the Richter scale, strong enough to cause widespread damage.
There were no immediate reports of injury or damage.
"All the people ran out into the streets in panic. Some were screaming and they are scared of further tremors," one witness said in northern Cyprus.
The tremor was also felt in Israel, Lebanon, Syria and Egypt.
An Egyptian seismologist from the Helwan Observatory said the epicentre was probably in the Gulf of Aqaba.
More than 500 people died and hundreds were hurt and left homeless when a strong earthquake hit Egypt on October 12, 1992. Most injuries occurred when badly constructed buildings collapsed.
In Cyprus, Wednesday's tremor lasted about a minute and telephone lines were jammed as residents sought information on the tremor and checked that friends and relatives were unharmed.
Cyprus radio reported the earthquake was felt throughout the island but especially in the southern coastal city of Limassol and the western resort of Paphos.
Its Paphos correspondent reported:"People in the commercial district ran into the streets. Drivers left the motors in their cars running and abandoned them."
In Cyprus, a mild second tremor was felt 50 minutes after the first which hit at 1310 GMT.
A Reuters correspondent in Tel Aviv described the tremor felt there as powerful.
"They evacuated the whole building. The floors shook," she said by mobile telephone outside the Reuters office in Tel Aviv. Palestinians in Gaza said they also felt the tremor.
